subject: mathematics
question_text: If sin θ = 4/5 and θ is not in the first quadrant, find the value of cos θ.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.106 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 164. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed VSAQ on its length and shape. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: AP 19. The mirror of the previous question. sin θ POSITIVE means Q1 or Q2; ruling out Q1 leaves Q2, where cos θ is negative. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Fix the quadrant
steps.margin_note: First mark. sin θ = 4/5 is positive, so θ is in Q1 or Q2. Q1 is ruled out, leaving Q2 — where cos θ is negative.
steps.memory_tip: sin positive means Q1 or Q2; Q1 is ruled out, so Q2 — where cos is NEGATIVE.
lines: sin θ = 4/5 is positive, so θ is in Q₁ or Q₂.
Since θ is not in Q₁, θ lies in Q₂.

recall.must_convey: That sin θ positive gives Q1 or Q2, Q1 is ruled out, so θ is in Q2 where cos θ is negative.
accept: sine is positive in the first and second quadrants and the first is ruled out so theta is in the second where cosine is negative
theta lies in the second quadrant so the cosine is negative
the quadrant fixes the sign as negative
Q one ruled out kabatti Q two, akkada cos negative

steps.why: Only the sine is given, and a sine value alone fits two different angles. The quadrant clause is what makes the answer unique.
common_mistakes: Assuming Q1 out of habit and writing 3/5.

steps.label: Find cos θ
steps.margin_note: Second mark. cos²θ = 1 − 16/25 = 9/25, so cos θ = ±3/5 — and the quadrant picks the minus.
steps.memory_tip: cos²θ = 9/25 gives ±3/5, and the quadrant picks the minus.

recall.must_convey: That cos²θ = 9/25 gives ±3/5, and the quadrant selects cos θ = −3/5.
accept: cos squared is nine over twenty five so cos theta is plus or minus three fifths and the quadrant picks minus three fifths
the answer is minus three by five
take the negative root because theta is in the second quadrant
nine by twenty five, so minus three fifths
cos theta is minus three fifths

steps.why: Writing ±3/5 and then choosing shows the examiner that the quadrant was used, rather than the right sign appearing by luck.
